source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 9 (India's Environmental Laws, Institutions and Programmes).

sections.heading: 1. Constitutional Provisions
points: **Article 48A (DPSP)** — the state shall protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
**Article 51A(g) (Fundamental Duty)** — every citizen's duty to protect the natural environment.
**Article 21 (Right to Life)** — courts have interpreted it to include the **right to a clean/healthy environment**.

sections.heading: 2. Major Environmental Laws
points: **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** — protects wildlife, sets up protected areas.
**Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974** — and set up the Pollution Control Boards.
**Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** — restricts diversion of forest land for non-forest use.
**Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**.
**Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — an umbrella act (enacted after Bhopal); empowers the Centre widely.
**Biological Diversity Act, 2002; Forest Rights Act, 2006; National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**.

sections.heading: 3. Institutions
points: **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** — nodal agency.
**Central & State Pollution Control Boards (CPCB/SPCB)** — monitor and control pollution.
**National Green Tribunal (NGT, 2010)** — a specialised court for speedy environmental justice.
**National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)**; **Wildlife Crime Control Bureau**; **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**.

sections.heading: 4. Programmes and Schemes
points: **Namami Gange** (river cleaning); **National Afforestation Programme**; **Compensatory Afforestation (CAMPA)**.
**Project Tiger, Project Elephant**; **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** with 8 missions.
**Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)** — mandatory clearance for major projects.
**Swachh Bharat** and waste management rules.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Art 48A (DPSP) + Art 51A(g) (duty) + Art 21 (right to clean environment).
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 = umbrella law (after Bhopal).
Forest Conservation Act (1980); Wildlife Protection Act (1972).
National Green Tribunal (NGT) = 2010; MoEFCC = nodal ministry.
EIA = clearance for major projects; Namami Gange = river cleaning.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** is the **umbrella** law, enacted after the **Bhopal** disaster.
**Art 48A = DPSP; Art 51A(g) = Fundamental Duty** (do not confuse).
The **NGT was established in 2010** (specialised environmental court).
**EIA** is required before clearance of major development projects.
